gaps.sentence: I look forward to ___ your suggestions at the meeting.
It started ___ just as we left the house.
gaps.explanation: start/begin take either -ing or to-infinitive; with continuous or states, 'to' is preferred. Both accepted.

gaps.sentence: They can't help ___ at his impression of the boss.
gaps.explanation: can't help + -ing = can't stop yourself: can't help laughing.

gaps.sentence: We mustn't miss ___ this exhibition — it ends on Sunday.
I was made ___ the dustbin lorry at six in the morning.
gaps.explanation: In the passive, make takes the to-infinitive: was made to wait.

gaps.sentence: She insisted on ___ for the meal herself.
Do you want me ___ you at the station?
gaps.explanation: want + object + to-infinitive: want me to meet.
